newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rubber - Japan prices seen drifting in ranges.
newsitem.headline: Rubber - Japan prices seen drifting in ranges.

text.p: Japanese rubber futures markets should drift in a narrow range this week, as expected softer prices for Thai benchmark rubber to Japan could offset recent falls in domestic rubber stocks, traders said on Monday.

"The market will be directionless. It will be hard for investors to take long or short positions because they expect the benchmark will be locked within ranges, perhaps between 141 yen and 144 yen in the near-term," a trading house trader said.
They said recent drops in domestic rubber stocks, combined with the yen's weaker tone, will make sellers reluctant to sell, but those factors would not be enough to push up prices.
The benchmark May contract on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) ended the morning session at 142.7 yen per kg, against 142.4 yen on Friday.
Similarly, the benchmark May contract on the Kobe Rubber Exchange was at 142.2 yen per kg, compared with 141.8 yen on Friday.
The offer price for Thai rubber to Japan was easier, quoted at around $1.22 per kg on a free-on-board basis on Monday, down from $1.25 on December 2.

Traders expect weaker prices in rubber producing countries this month due to slack tyre demand from the United States and Europe ahead of the Christmas holidays, adding the factor could cap any price rebound here.

Japan's rubber stocks at designated warehouses at the end of November amounted to 39,698 tonnes, the first time they had fallen below 40,000 tonnes since mid-August, according to the Rubber Trade Association of Japan.
However, recent static rubber futures prices have dulled private investor interest in the futures markets.
